Runtime.0002.description:
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
Runtime.0002.title: Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience

links.title: Upgrade to latest .NET with Upgrade Assistant

Database.0002.description:
SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
    1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
    2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
    3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.
Database.0002.title: SQL database connection detected

links.title: Migrate SQL Server database to Azure

Database.0003.description:
System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.
Database.0003.title: System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected

Security.0002.description:
Connection strings without configuration builders detected.  

 Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.). 

 Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.
Security.0002.title: Connection strings without configuration builders detected

Scale.0001.description:
Static content detected.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Scale.0001.title: Static content detected

Local.0003.description:
Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
    1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
    2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
    3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local.0003.title: Local or network IO operations detected

Local.0007.description:
Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
Local.0007.title: Local OS environment access detected

links.title: App Service sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps

Local.0006.description:
Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local.0006.title: Hardcoded URLs detected

security.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json
security.description: [CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): HIGH severity denial of service from deeply nested JSON. Newtonsoft.Json 6.0.4 is within affected range < 13.0.1; upgrade to 13.0.1 or later supported release. Dependency vulnerability is confirmed, not remote exploitability. GitHub advisories queried for all three distinct manifest packages (also EntityFramework 6.1.3 and Microsoft.AspNet.WebApi.Client 5.2.3); withdrawn duplicate GHSA-8rfx-6mr3-5jh3 excluded. Coverage limitation: dotnet list package --include-transitive --format json failed because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets is missing. Fallback inspected packages.config and project references; transitive/runtime dependency completeness is not guaranteed.

security.title: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
security.description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems loops over every service-provided item and loads/decodes/resizes one image per iteration without a count bound. CatalogService permits adding items and returns all matching items without paging. A large catalog drives excessive UI-thread work and unresponsiveness. Availability/code-quality finding; no infinite loop or demonstrated unauthenticated remote exploit is claimed.

security.title: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
security.description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems converts decimal monetary Price to double through a string, losing precision for valid SQL money/decimal values. Verified using .NET numeric conversion: 900000000000000.01 renders as 900000000000000.00 after double parsing and F2 formatting, even with zero discount. This amount is within the SQL money range used by CatalogItem.Price and decimal(19,4) precision configuration. This affects displayed monetary calculations; no payment authorization effect established.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems allocates Image img using Image.FromFile and creates a thumbnail, but never disposes the original image after thumbnail generation. Each catalog refresh repeats these allocations and retains native image resources until eventual finalization. Thumbnail disposal when rows are cleared is also not explicit. This is a resource-lifetime/availability issue, not unmanaged memory corruption.

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems does not dispose the Image returned by Image.FromFile after producing its thumbnail. Image.FromFile keeps the source file locked until Image disposal; subsequent refreshes therefore leave file/native image handles awaiting finalization rather than releasing them at effective lifetime end. Same underlying image-lifetime issue as CWE-772.

security.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
security.description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.GetCatalogItems calls ents.CatalogItems.ToList() before filtering and then allocates another list. CreateCatalogItem allows caller-provided records to grow the table without an application count limit. Result allocation scales with caller-influenced database cardinality rather than a bounded page, permitting excessive memory use for large catalogs. This is an availability pattern, not a measured memory exhaustion exploit; infrastructure quotas and WCF transport limits were not tested.

security.title: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
security.description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem reads the shared database MAX(Id), increments it, and inserts in a separate SaveChanges operation without synchronization spanning the read/allocate/write sequence. Id explicitly uses DatabaseGeneratedOption.None. Concurrent requests handled by different service instances can read the same maximum, choose the same primary key and cause one insert to fail. CreateAvailableStock repeats this pattern for StockId and has a non-atomic existence check. A per-instance WCF single-concurrency default does not serialize all service instances. Database constraints may reject a conflicting write but do not make allocation atomic. CWE-567/662/820 describe the same missing-synchronization root cause, not three independent vulnerabilities. No concurrent execution test performed.

security.title: Improper Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem reads the shared database MAX(Id), increments it, and inserts in a separate SaveChanges operation without synchronization spanning the read/allocate/write sequence. Id explicitly uses DatabaseGeneratedOption.None. Concurrent requests handled by different service instances can read the same maximum, choose the same primary key and cause one insert to fail. CreateAvailableStock repeats this pattern for StockId and has a non-atomic existence check. A per-instance WCF single-concurrency default does not serialize all service instances. Database constraints may reject a conflicting write but do not make allocation atomic. CWE-567/662/820 describe the same missing-synchronization root cause, not three independent vulnerabilities. No concurrent execution test performed.

security.title: Missing Synchronization
security.description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem reads the shared database MAX(Id), increments it, and inserts in a separate SaveChanges operation without synchronization spanning the read/allocate/write sequence. Id explicitly uses DatabaseGeneratedOption.None. Concurrent requests handled by different service instances can read the same maximum, choose the same primary key and cause one insert to fail. CreateAvailableStock repeats this pattern for StockId and has a non-atomic existence check. A per-instance WCF single-concurrency default does not serialize all service instances. Database constraints may reject a conflicting write but do not make allocation atomic. CWE-567/662/820 describe the same missing-synchronization root cause, not three independent vulnerabilities. No concurrent execution test performed.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem and RemoveCatalogItem modify persistent catalog data and call SaveChanges without recording actor, operation, target or outcome. No application audit logger or configured WCF audit behavior was found. Consequently security-relevant changes cannot be attributed using application audit records. External IIS/database monitoring might exist but was not provided and cannot be inferred.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems concatenates service-provided Picturefilename into the catalog image directory and passes it to Image.FromFile without canonicalization or containment checking. Relative .. segments can escape that intended directory. CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem/UpdateCatalogItem persist supplied model filenames. Impact is loading an accessible image outside the catalog directory; arbitrary file disclosure or code execution is not established.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems concatenates service-provided Picturefilename into the catalog image directory and passes it to Image.FromFile without canonicalization or containment checking. Relative .. segments can escape that intended directory. CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem/UpdateCatalogItem persist supplied model filenames. Impact is loading an accessible image outside the catalog directory; arbitrary file disclosure or code execution is not established.

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.

evidence.explanation: CatalogView.SetCatalogItems uses the upstream service Picturefilename as part of a local image resource identifier without directory containment checks. CatalogService accepts and persists this field. Relative traversal can select an accessible image outside the intended catalog directory. This is the same underlying path issue as CWE-22/23, not an independent exploit.
